summary.goal: Replace flat plan listing with attention-based navigation that surfaces actionable items, organizes active work, and provides quick access to the full catalog - enabling 'Inbox Zero' mental model at scale.
summary.context: Currently /plans shows a simple list with status filters. At scale (hundreds/thousands of plans), users need attention-based organization that surfaces what needs action, not just taxonomy. The system already has rich attention signals: change requests, pending gates, submitted drafts, execution status, comments - these should drive navigation priority.

acceptance_criteria.description: Plans list page shows 'Needs Attention' section at top with actionable items grouped by attention type
Plans list page shows 'Working On' section with user's active drafts and running executions
Plans list page shows collapsible 'All Plans' section with scope grouping
Each attention item shows clear action indicator and time context
Attention counts are visible in section headers
Empty attention state shows encouraging message, not error
Navigation remains fast with large plan counts (pagination/virtualization where needed)
